post.caption: A gold coin with no face value. South Africa first struck the Krugerrand on July 3, 1967. It holds one troy ounce of pure gold, and the coin is 22 karat, so the copper in it makes it harder and slightly reddish. It has no face value, so its worth is its gold. Paul Kruger, a South African president, is on one side and a leaping springbok on the other. The British gold sovereign uses the same 22 karat alloy. The Krugerrand was made so ordinary people could invest in gold, and in 1978 more than six million were struck.
